about: Behavior check (guard/behavior): without running the code, recover values (constant folding, decoding, name assembly) and follow how they flow to turn 'what it does and when' into facts; this table then sets the verdict. The vocabulary below applies only to recovered values (paths, hosts, commands), not to text patterns. Phase: auto = install, interpreter start, import (runs without the user calling anything); call = inside a function (runs only when something calls it). null = kept as evidence only, not used for the verdict.

download_exec.label: Runs downloaded content
download_exec.text: Runs content (or a file) fetched from the network
download_exec.benign: Installers that download and run a platform binary (npm install scripts such as esbuild)

decode_exec.label: Runs decoded code
decode_exec.text: Unpacks hidden (encoded or compressed) code and runs it
decode_exec.benign: Code generators or serialization libraries that unpack and run their own data (rare)

secret_exfil.label: Sends secrets out
secret_exfil.text: Reads credential files, browser or wallet storage, or the whole environment and sends it out
secret_exfil.benign: SDKs and publish tools that send a credential to its own service (twine, docker login), only in code inside functions

suspicious_send.label: Sends data to a suspicious address
suspicious_send.text: Sends user or system info to a webhook, collector service or bare IP address

sysinfo_beacon.label: Sends system info at install or import
sysinfo_beacon.text: Sends info such as user name, host name or working directory out when it runs
sysinfo_beacon.benign: Tools that send install statistics (rare, usually with user consent)

persistence.label: Registers itself to run automatically
persistence.text: Adds itself to startup programs, shell startup files, services or scheduled tasks
persistence.benign: CLIs that install shell completion (inside a function the user calls)

remote_shell.label: Remote shell
remote_shell.text: Connects a shell to an outside server

hidden_call.label: Calls a built-in under a hidden name
hidden_call.text: Assembles or hides the name of an exec function before calling it (a pattern that evades analysis)
hidden_call.benign: Compatibility code that picks a built-in with getattr

unreadable_exec.label: Runs code that cannot be read
unreadable_exec.text: At install or import, runs a value that analysis cannot recover as code or a command
unreadable_exec.benign: Plugin loaders that run code read from config

install_process.label: Runs an external command during install
install_process.text: The install script runs a program that is not a build tool
install_process.benign: setup.py calling a build tool missing from the build list

install_runs_unread.label: Install runs a file that was not read
install_runs_unread.text: The install script runs or exec()s a file (a build script, a data file) that is too large to read or that the package does not ship
install_runs_unread.benign: Builds that run a very large or generated build script

not_analyzed.label: Code that runs by itself was not analyzed
not_analyzed.text: A file that runs at install, interpreter start or import went over an analysis limit (size, steps, time, number of files) and was not (fully) read
not_analyzed.benign: Very large packages: generated modules, vendored libraries

wipe.label: Deletes the user's or the system's files
wipe.text: Removes or overwrites the home folder, something in it, a drive or a system folder (rm -rf ~/..., shutil.rmtree, mkfs, dd to a disk)
wipe.benign: Uninstall or cleanup helpers that remove their own folder in the home directory (inside a function the user calls)

encoded_source.label: Code hidden behind its source encoding
encoded_source.text: A Python file declares a source encoding (utf-7, unicode_escape ...) that turns plain-looking text into different code
